The sources indicate that 24 Mantra, a D2C brand, faces reputation problems and criticism, particularly in the context of health supplements in India where establishing trust is challenging due to skepticism and lack of education about supplement benefits. The sources also mention that D2C brands in general struggle with maintaining trust and overcoming negative reviews, and The Honest Company, another D2C brand, faced reputation issues due to class action lawsuits and product recalls. Additionally, Everlane was accused of targeting unionization efforts, which affected its reputation. The difficulties faced in this regard include reducing the effects of negative reviews and building a positive reputation. When it comes to purchasing decisions, consumers value safety, efficacy, and trust. D2C brands must overcome these challenges while simultaneously developing a compelling value proposition that appeals to their target market. Customers in India tend to prefer buying health supplements from reputable brick-and-mortar retailers.

Navigating Price Sensitivity [...] Healthcare D2C brands must dispel false information in order to combat consumer skepticism about supplements, which is particularly pervasive among Indian consumers due to a lack of education about their use. The lack of concrete evidence of product quality and compliance makes it challenging to establish trust.
